headline: NHRC, India’s fifth ITEC Executive capacity-building programme on human rights in partnership with the MEA for senior functionaries of NHRIs of the Global South, begins in New Delhi
fullText:
National Human Rights Commission

NHRC, India’s fifth ITEC Executive capacity-building programme on human rights in partnership with the MEA for senior functionaries of NHRIs of the Global South, begins in New Delhi

Inaugurating the six-day programme, NHRC, India Chairperson, Justice Shri V. Ramasubramanian, says shifting social values in a rapidly changing world pose serious challenges to human rights

Highlights emerging technologies raising questions on the Right to life after death, Right to be forgotten or Right to erasure, presenting both challenges and potential advantages for human life

In this backdrop, platforms such as the ITEC Capacity Building Programme on Human Rights initiated by NHRC, India acquire significance

14 SEP 2026 8:23PM by PIB Delhi

The fifth Indian Technical and Economic Cooperation (ITEC) Executive Capacity Building Programme on Human Rights for National Human Rights Institutions (NHRIs) of the Global South, organised by the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC), India, in partnership with the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA), began in New Delhi today.

About 38 participants from NHRIs of 14 countries of the Global South are participating in the programme. The participating countries are Algeria, Chile, Ecuador, Ethiopia, Indonesia, Kazakhstan, Kenya, Kyrgyzstan, Malaysia, Oman, Samoa, South Africa, Tajikistan and Zimbabwe.

Chairperson, NHRC, India Justice V. Ramasubramanian, in his inaugural address highlighted India’s longstanding and excellent relations with the participating countries. He said that the programme aims to share knowledge and apply it for the betterment of society. He emphasised that India has a long tradition of promoting and sharing noble thoughts for achieving the common goal of human welfare.

In this context, he referred to the ancient Indian traditions reflected in the Rigveda and Taittiriya Upanishad of the Yajurveda. He also referred to the ancient Greek concept known as Xenia, which casts a responsibility on hosts to respect their guests and on guests to share their knowledge.

The Chairperson acknowledged the various constitutional frameworks for promoting and protecting human rights in the participating countries. He expressed hope that the participants would find the programme enriching and meaningful, develop a lasting association with NHRC, India and continue their engagement with the Commission.

Later, addressing the first session after the inauguration, Justice Ramasubramanian said that shifting social values in a rapidly changing world are posing serious challenges to human rights. He observed that over the last 100 years, the very concept of family has undergone significant change, to the point that questions are now being raised about whether the family means only a man and a woman.

He also highlighted third and fourth-generation rights and the challenges posed to human rights by emerging technologies, including synthetic technology, industrial technology, genome technology and digital technology. Justice Ramasubramanian noted that questions relating to the right to life after death, the right to be forgotten or the right to erasure are being discussed both as challenges and as potential advantages for human life.

Referring to the 2025 Global Peace Index of the Sydney-based international think tank, the Institute for Economics and Peace, the Chairperson said that 78 countries in the world are currently engaged in armed conflicts outside their borders. These conflicts resulted in severe consequences for human civilisation and the global economy, displacing nearly 122 million people as refugees or internally displaced persons and causing an estimated loss of about 20 trillion dollars to the global economy.

He emphasised that it is in this context that the true meaning and importance of human rights must be understood. Against this backdrop, he said, platforms such as the ITEC Capacity Building Programme on Human Rights initiated by NHRC, India, acquire significance.

During the inaugural session, NHRC, India Member, Justice (Dr.) Bidyut Ranjan Sarangi emphasised the need to consider the meaning and purpose of the capacity-building programme carefully. He underscored the importance of continuing friendship and cooperation, particularly as the international community passes through a critical period and reiterated the need to sustain the spirit of peace and dialogue.

Welcoming representatives from different countries, he observed that such interactions provide an encouraging platform for greater understanding and cooperation. He called for collective efforts to work together and do better for the world, expressing hope for a more peaceful and harmonious future.

NHRC, India Member, Smt. Vijaya Bharathi Sayani invoked the philosophy of Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam – the world as one family – as the ethos binding the participants together. Highlighting India’s scale and diversity, she noted that the country, despite its vast population, 22 official languages, diverse religious traditions and varied customs and festivals across its 28 States and eight Union Territories, remains united and stable through its culture of pluralism.

She urged respect for differing viewpoints and emphasised the protection of the vulnerable and the dignity of every individual as enduring civilisational values. She affirmed compassion, accountability and equity as the guiding principles of the Commission in its role as guardian of the rights of every individual.

NHRC, India Secretary General, Shri Piyush Goyal welcomed the Chairpersons, delegates and representatives of the 14 NHRIs attending the fifth edition of the programme. He highlighted the steady growth of the ITEC initiative since its first edition in 2023 and noted that it has continuously evolved based on feedback from previous years to make it more useful for participating institutions.

He highlighted the practical orientation of the programme, comprising lectures, thematic sessions, interactive discussions, presentations by resource persons, country presentations and field visits. He encouraged delegates to engage with resource persons and one another, drawing on the experience of institutions operating within different legal frameworks.

NHRC, India Joint Secretary, Shri Samir Kumar extended a warm welcome to all participants and stated that the ITEC programme is conceived not merely as capacity building, but as a foundation for friendship, professional exchange and lasting partnership among NHRIs of the Global South. He emphasised that bringing together colleagues from different institutional backgrounds provides an opportunity to find common ground and strengthen one another’s institutions.

In the Vote of Thanks proposed by NHRC, India Joint Secretary, Smt. Saidingpuii Chhakchuak, the support received from the MEA in organising the programme and the collaborative participation of the delegates were given a warm acknowledgement.

headline: INDIAN AIR FORCE DRONATHON - 2026
fullText:
Ministry of Defence

INDIAN AIR FORCE DRONATHON - 2026

14 SEP 2026 8:01PM by PIB Delhi

Air Marshal Ashutosh Dixit, Vice Chief of the Air Staff, inaugurated the first Indian Air Force Dronathon-2026 at the Pokhran Field Firing Range, Jaisalmer, today. The inaugural ceremony was attended by senior functionaries of MoD, HQ IDS and representatives from Indian Army, and BSF. Dronathon-2026 is an IAF initiative aimed at engaging directly with the Indian unmanned systems industry and assessing emerging technologies under realistic operational conditions. The three-day event, planned from 14 to 16 September 2026, brings together over 20 leading defence companies, start-ups MSMEs, DPSUs and innovators from India's rapidly evolving unmanned systems ecosystem.

The IAF views unmanned systems as an important complement to manned aviation providing commanders with additional options to enhance the reach, persistence responsiveness and flexibility of air operations During the Dronathon, participating companies and innovators will demonstrate their Unmanned Aircraft Systems (UAS) and associated technologies at the Pokhran range.

The demonstrations will encompass a wide spectrum of operational capabilities including surveillance and reconnaissance, autonomous operations, swarm technologies, electronic warfare and Counter-Unmanned Aircraft Systems (CUAS). The central focus of Dronathon-2026 is to move from technology demonstration to operational effect. The systems are being assessed for their reliability, and effectiveness in demanding and contested environments, as well as their ability to adapt to evolving operational requirements and emerging threats.

During the event today, the VCAS also released the ‘IAF UAS Roadmap’, providing greater clarity to Indian industry on capability priorities. The roadmap is intended to facilitate focused innovation and enable the unmanned airborne systems industry, academia and research organisations to align their efforts with the future requirements of the IAF.

On the opening day of Dronathon-2026, the Indian Air Force successfully demonstrated a key capability of "Vayu UTtaM," its indigenously developed multi-mode Unmanned Traffic Management (UTM) system. During its real time demonstration at Pokhran, it detected and tracked both military and civil UAS. The capability is designed to facilitate coordinated management of UAS operations in increasingly congested airspace, while also supporting the identification and timely mitigation of unauthorised or rogue drones. With the increasing proliferation of UAS, Vayu UTtaM has potential applications beyond the military domain, including in areas related to airspace safety, critical infrastructure, civil aviation and public safety.

Dronathon-2026 reinforces the IAF's commitment to Atmanirbharta in unmanned systems, with the focus extending beyond airframes to the complete ecosystem, including propulsion, sensors and payloads, communications, autonomy, electronic warfare, countermeasures and airspace management.

headline: NHRC, India’s two-week Online Short-Term Internship Programme in September 2026 begins
fullText:
National Human Rights Commission

NHRC, India’s two-week Online Short-Term Internship Programme in September 2026 begins

100 university-level students from diverse academic backgrounds shortlisted out of more than one thousand applicants

Chairperson, Justice V. Ramasubramanian urges interns to reflect on the purpose behind joining the internship to make the best use of its learning opportunities

Member, Justice (Dr.) Bidyut Ranjan Sarangi says, understanding essence of human rights necessary to help the interns in life

Member, Vijaya Bharathi Sayani urges interns to go beyond the theoretical understanding of law and observe, listen, question, analyse and act with sensitivity at the grassroots level

Secretary General, Shri Piyush Goyal describes human rights as a broad and nuanced domain and urges the interns to understand its diverse dimensions

14 SEP 2026 7:56PM by PIB Delhi

The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC), India’s two-week Online Short-Term Internship Programme (OSTI) for university students in September 2026 began today at Manav Adhikar Bhawan, New Delhi. NHRC, India Chairperson, Justice V. Ramasubramanian, inaugurated the programme in the presence of NHRC, India Members, Justice (Dr.) Bidyut Ranjan Sarangi and Smt. Vijaya Bharathi Sayani, Secretary General Shri Piyush Goyal, Joint Secretary Smt. Saidingpuii Chhakchhuak and Deputy Secretary Smt. Vineetha Ottapurakkal Kallada. A total of 100 students from diverse academic backgrounds, selected from over 1,000 applicants, are participating in the programme.

Addressing the interns, Justice V. Ramasubramanian urged them to reflect on the purpose behind joining the internship to make the best use of its learning opportunities. He said that the programme would achieve its purpose if the interns learnt to look at society through a human rights lens. Observing that the same news can have different interpretations, he emphasised the importance of knowledge and awareness which helps in informed understanding of situations to make meaningful contribution to society.

NHRC, India Member, Justice (Dr.) Bidyut Ranjan Sarangi said that understanding the essence of human rights is necessary to help the interns in life. He said while the interns possess knowledge, gaining experience is essential to applying human rights values meaningfully at every stage of life.

NHRC, India Member, Smt. Vijaya Bharathi Sayani emphasised that every individual has the right to live with dignity. She urged the interns to go beyond the theoretical understanding of law and observe, listen, question, analyse and act with sensitivity at the grassroots level. Justice, Equality, Liberty and Fraternity, she said, should become lived values and not remain merely words in the Preamble of the Constitution. She also encouraged the interns to learn both from law and from people.

NHRC, India Secretary General, Shri Piyush Goyal described human rights as a broad and nuanced domain and urged the interns to understand its diverse dimensions, work collectively and contribute towards strengthening human dignity. He wished them a successful and fulfilling internship.

NHRC, India Joint Secretary, Smt. SaidingpuiiChhakchhuak gave an overview of the two-week programme, which will feature around 30 lectures by 20 eminent speakers, including senior government officials, academicians, civil society representatives, human rights defenders, NHRC officers, representatives of international institutions and subject experts. The interns will also undertake virtual visits to places such as police station, Tihar Prison etc. to understand their functioning and challenges.

14 SEP 2026 7:54PM by PIB Delhi

H.E. Imaan Sulaiman-Ibrahim, fsi, Minister of Women Affairs and Social Development, Federal Republic of Nigeria, met the Union Minister for Women and Child Development, Government of India, Smt. Annpurna Devi, today in New Delhi at the Ministry of Women and Child Development, GPOA,New Delhi.

The two Ministers also discussed areas of mutual interest, including clean energy, social protection and national care systems. She stated that she looks forward to knowledge exchange and to learning from India's best practices, including in the areas of women's collectives and skilling, financing women's entrepreneurship, nutrition support, women-led governance and the care economy.

The two Ministers expressed the view that the two countries can work together on the areas of women's economic collectives and clean energy, social protection and the care economy, and child rights, protection and digital inclusion, and expressed hope that the meeting would strengthen and enhance the long standing relations between the two countries.

headline: Ministry Of Social Justice And Empowerment Strengthens Educational Empowerment Through Scholarships And Digital Reforms
fullText:
Ministry of Statistics & Programme Implementation

Ministry Of Social Justice And Empowerment Strengthens Educational Empowerment Through Scholarships And Digital Reforms

Rs 4,893.03 Crore Released Under Pre-Matric Scholarships And Rs 46,581.54 Crore Under Post-Matric Scholarships For SC Students During FY 2014–15 To FY 2025–26

DBT, Aadhaar-Based Authentication, Digital Verification Strengthen Transparency And Scholarship Delivery

14 SEP 2026 7:15PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Social Justice and Empowerment, Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, has undertaken targeted interventions to strengthen equitable access to education for Scheduled Castes (SCs), Other Backward Classes (OBCs), Economically Backward Classes (EBCs) and Denotified, Nomadic and Semi-Nomadic Tribes (DNTs).

Secretary, Ministry of Social Justice And Empowerment Shri Sudhansh Pant said that the Department is supporting educational continuity and reducing financial barriers for socially and educationally disadvantaged communities, through scholarships, residential infrastructure, overseas education assistance, fellowships, coaching initiatives and digital reforms.

Shri Pant said these interventions seek to improve access to quality institutions and support students across different stages of education. He added that specific emphasis has been placed on transparent scholarship delivery, beneficiary authentication and Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT)-enabled systems.

The Secretary informed that the Pre-Matric Scholarships Scheme for Scheduled Castes and Others is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme aimed at promoting literacy, reducing dropout rates and ensuring continuity of education at the pre-matric level. It supports children belonging to Scheduled Castes and children of parents or guardians engaged in unclean and hazardous occupations. He said through targeted financial assistance, the scheme strengthens educational inclusion and helps students from disadvantaged backgrounds continue their school education.

Shri Pant informed that during FY 2014–15 to FY 2025–26, Central Assistance amounting to Rs 4,893.03 Crore was released under the scheme, with reported annual beneficiary figures totalling approximately 299.66 lakh over the period. During FY 2025–26 alone, Rs 562.36 Crore was released, benefiting 26.79 lakh students, he added.

Stating that the Post-Matric Scholarship Scheme for Scheduled Caste students is a flagship Centrally Sponsored intervention, the Secretary said that Scheme is designed to improve access to higher education among students from economically disadvantaged SC households. He added that the Scheme seeks to reduce financial barriers in post-secondary education, strengthen retention and enhance the Gross Enrolment Ratio of SC students in higher education institutions.

The Secretary further informed that during FY 2014–15 to FY 2025–26, Central Assistance amounting to Rs 46,581.54 Crore was released under the scheme, with reported annual beneficiary figures totalling 612.98 lakh over the period. During FY 2025–26, Central Assistance of Rs 6,186.95 crore was released, benefiting 47.53 lakh students.

Digital Reforms Strengthen Transparency and Beneficiary Authentication

Describing digital reforms to strengthen transparency and authentication, Shri Pant said that from FY 2021–22 onwards, the Department transitioned the Post-Matric Scholarship Scheme to a DBT-enabled framework, facilitating direct transfer of scholarship assistance into Aadhaar-seeded bank accounts of beneficiaries. He said this reform has strengthened accountability, reduced delays and leakages, and improved last-mile delivery.

The Secretary further stated that the Department has introduced de-duplication mechanisms to identify and eliminate fake and duplicate beneficiaries, alongside biometric authentication and e-KYC-based verification of beneficiaries and officials. Integration with DigiLocker and API SETU facilitates digital verification of certificates and documents, he added.

Shri Pant informed that One-Time Registration has been introduced to enable tracking of beneficiaries across schemes and academic years. He said integration with AISHE, UDISE, NCVT and SCVT databases supports validation of institutional and student records, while multi-layered checks help minimize discrepancies and duplication.

The Secretary said linkages with UIDAI, NPCI and PFMS further support seamless processing and direct disbursement of scholarship assistance which strengthen beneficiary authentication, improve fund-flow management and support a more transparent and accountable scholarship delivery system.

The Secretary expressed hope that through sustained financial assistance and technology-enabled reforms, the Department would continue to strengthen educational opportunities for disadvantaged communities, supporting students in continuing their education and accessing higher learning.

headline: Unusual wave-like heat transport in crystalline solid signals breakthrough converting waste heat in industries
fullText:
Ministry of Science & Technology

Unusual wave-like heat transport in crystalline solid signals breakthrough converting waste heat in industries

14 SEP 2026 5:59PM by PIB Delhi

An unusual heat transport regime detected in a newly studied copper chalcogenide material called thallium copper selenide (TlCu5Se3) could pave way for efficient conversion of waste heat to electricity via thermoelectric energy conversion in power plants, cement industries, steel plants, automobiles, data centres and battery heat management systems.

Conventional superionic materials can achieve low lattice thermal conductivity via highly mobile ions. But excessive ion migration may cause structural instability and compromise its thermoelectric performance. Confined ion diffusion, where ionic motion remains restricted within a complex crystalline framework, offers a way to suppress heat transport while preserving structural stability and promoting unconventional heat-transport mechanisms.

In crystalline materials, heat is conventionally understood to be transported by particle-like phonons, with phonon mean free path (MFP) typically much larger than the interatomic distance. In contrast, strong disorder and anharmonicity (phenomenon in which atomic vibrations become asymmetric and deviate significantly from normal parabolic behaviour, disrupting propagation of heat) in glasses reduce the MFP to nearly the interatomic length scale, suppressing conventional phonon propagation.

This conventional picture, however, becomes increasingly inadequate when strong anharmonicity and structural disorder can retain long-range crystallographic order while exhibiting highly localized, closely spaced vibrational modes that interact strongly with one another.

In this intermediate regime, thermal energy can be transported not only through particle-like phonon propagation but also through wave-like coherence between different vibrational modes, enabling ultralow lattice thermal conductivity. Such ultralow thermal conducting materials have immense importance in thermal barrier coatings, thermoelectric energy conversion, thermal decoherence free quantum technology.

Researchers at Jawaharlal Nehru Centre for Advanced Scientific Research (JNCASR), Bengaluru (an autonomous institution under the Department of Science & Technology, Govt. of India) and other research team members have found an unusual wave-like thermal transport regime in a newly studied copper chalcogenide material, TlCu5Se3 that can lead to high-performance thermoelectric conversion.

The complex crystal framework of TlCu5Se3 was expected to restrict the motion of Cu atoms rather than allowing long-range migration providing opportunity to investigate whether this confined dynamic behaviour could generate strong anharmonicity and suppress heat transport without causing structural instability.

In this work, led by Prof. Kanishka Biswas and his Ph.D. students, Ms. Sayantoni Choudhury and Dr. Animesh Bhui from the New Chemistry Unit (NCU) at JNCASR, published in the prestigious journal, Science Advances, investigated the structural and thermoelectric properties through experiments and conducted advanced theoretical calculations to understand the origin of the unusual heat transport.

They showed that the complex crystal structure and intrinsically confined dynamic disorder of the Cu sublattice generate exceptionally strong anharmonicity, leading to predominantly wave-like phonon transport and an intrinsically ultralow lattice thermal conductivity.

Fig 1: A schematic illustrating the complex knot-like structural framework that leads to a confined Cu dynamic, resulting in unusual heat transport and ultrahigh thermoelectric performance in TlCu5Se3.

This unusual thermal transport, together with favorable electronic transport, give rise to one of the highest thermoelectric performances (thermoelectric figure of merit, zT of 1.7) among pristine ternary chalcogenides. The origin of this unusual behaviour lies in the distinctive crystal framework of TlCu5Se3. The compound crystallizes in a tetragonal structure and forms a complex three-dimensional cloverleaf knot-like framework with open channels along the crystallographic c-axis.

The intrinsic bonding hierarchy associated with this complex framework leads to these confined dynamics. To probe the presence of this confined dynamic behaviour of Cu, the team collaborated with Prof. Umesh V. Waghmare and his postdoc Dr. Prasad V. Matukumilli from the Theoretical Sciences Unit (TSU), JNCASR, Bengaluru, to perform advanced first-principles theoretical calculations and molecular-dynamics simulations.

Fig 2: Prof. Kanishka Biswas (left) and Sayantoni Choudhury (right) JNCASR, Bangalore.

Molecular-dynamics simulations (computer simulations of atomic motions over time) reveal that Cu atoms exhibit localized dynamic disorder rather than the long-range, liquid-like diffusion characteristic of superionic copper chalcogenides. This confined motion acts primarily as a source of strong lattice anharmonicity. As a direct consequence, heat begins to propagate through wave-like coherence, with phonons tunnelling between localized vibrational states rather than moving as well-defined particles. To uncover how these unusual vibrations transport heat, the researchers went beyond the conventional phonon-gas model and employed the unified formalism of thermal transport. This framework considers both particle-like phonon propagation and wave-like coherence between different phonon branches.

The significance of this work extends beyond thermoelectric performance, which establishes how structural complexity and confined ion dynamics can lead to an unconventional mechanism for thermal management and high-performance thermoelectric energy conversion.

Publication link: DOI:10.1126/sciadv.aeh9096

(Release ID: 2310168)

headline: Department of Rural Development and PFRDA Sign MoU to Expand Pension Coverage in Rural India Through ‘Pension Sakhis’
fullText:
Ministry of Rural Development

Department of Rural Development and PFRDA Sign MoU to Expand Pension Coverage in Rural India Through ‘Pension Sakhis’

15 SEP 2026 8:54AM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Rural Development (DoRD) and the Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA) signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to expand pension coverage and strengthen social security among rural households through a dedicated cadre of ‘Pension Sakhis’.

The partnership will leverage the community institutional network of Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana-National Rural Livelihoods Mission, including Banking Correspondent (BC) Sakhis and other trained community resource persons, to raise awareness, facilitate enrolment, and provide pension-related support to Self Help Group (SHG) members, rural women, Lakhpati Didis, and other underserved groups. These cadres will provide doorstep awareness, enrolment, and support in remote areas. Digital dashboards, mobile- and web-based solutions, and unique identifier-based tracking through Central Recordkeeping Agencies will support monitoring of outreach, enrolment, and performance.

Shri Rohit Kansal, Secretary, Ministry of Rural Development, in his keynote address, mentioned that SHG members have distinct savings patterns, livelihood cycles, and risk profiles. He highlighted that social security is an integral pillar of the Mission’s vision of inclusive growth, helping SHG households manage vulnerabilities, build resilience, and move towards greater and sustained prosperity. He stressed that pension awareness and financial literacy must be built on honesty, transparency, and trust, and expressed confidence that trained BC Sakhis and other financially literate community cadres could serve as Pension Sakhis to expand pension coverage across rural India.

Ms. Mamta Shankar, Whole Time Member (Economics), PFRDA highlighted the need for retirement planning amid rising life expectancy and changing demographic trends. She was hopeful that the collaboration would promote the adoption of pension products, including the National Pension System (NPS), among rural households with limited access to formal retirement and social security mechanisms.

Shri Amit Shukla, Joint Secretary, RL (I), Mrs. Swati Sharma, Joint Secretary, RL (II) and Ms. Sumeet Kaur Kapoor, Executive Director, PFRDA, were also present on the occasion. The DoRD reaffirmed its commitment of supporting the implementation of the MoU and facilitating the deployment of Pension Sakhis across the country.

Both DoRD and PFRDA expressed confidence that the partnership would strengthen pension literacy, deepen financial inclusion, and enhance social protection for rural communities. The collaboration is expected to contribute significantly in building a more inclusive and resilient social security ecosystem through greater financial security for rural citizens across the country.

headline: CSIR-NIScPR Leverages SARAL AI to Take Scientific Research to Wider Audiences

Ministry of Science & Technology

CSIR-NIScPR Leverages SARAL AI to Take Scientific Research to Wider Audiences

15 SEP 2026 8:46AM by PIB Delhi

The CSIR-National Institute of Science Communication and Policy Research (CSIR-NIScPR) has taken a new step towards strengthening science communication by leveraging SARAL AI: an initiative of Anusandhan National Research Foundation (ANRF) New Delhi to convert research published in its journals into engaging and accessible videos.

The initiative is in line with the Government’s emphasis on adoption of emerging technologies for effective communication of science and research. Dr Jitendra Singh, Hon’ble Minister for Science & Technology, has recently encouraged the institutes to use SARAL AI, with CSIR-NIScPR emerging as a leading organisation in its adoption.

Under the leadership of Dr. Geetha Vani Rayasam, Director, CSIR-NIScPR, the Institute has been actively exploring new-age technologies and digital platforms to expand the reach and impact of science communication. As part of this effort, NIScPR organised a hands-on workshop on SARAL AI recently, with participation from more than 90 participants including editors of the journals and researchers. Dr. Geetha Vani Rayasam, Director, CSIR-NIScPR, said, “Scientific knowledge creates greater value when it reaches beyond the research community. By embracing new-age technologies such as SARAL AI, CSIR-NIScPR is working to make Indian research more accessible and reach wider and more diverse audiences.”

The initiative draws impetus from the Anusandhan National Research Foundation (ANRF)’s emphasis on promoting wider dissemination of scientific knowledge and making research more accessible to society. During a visit to NIScPR, Dr. Shivkumar Kalyanaraman, CEO, ANRF, highlighted about the SARAL AI, a tool for making short videos from the research papers published. He encouraged the Institute to explore SARAL AI as a tool to simplify complex scientific research and communicate it effectively to the common public. Dr. Shivkumar Kalyanaraman, CEO, ANRF, said, “Research should not stop with publication. Tools such as SARAL AI can help researchers and institutions take their work beyond papers, make it accessible to many more people, and amplify the impact of Indian research.”

This initiative is aimed at making scientific research easier to discover, understand and share, particularly among students and the general public. The videos are being made available through a dedicated YouTube playlist (YouTube Playlist Link- https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLb4FmdATtzOs ), providing an additional digital pathway for research to reach audiences beyond the traditional research papers.

headline: SHREYAS Strengthens Higher Education Opportunities for SC and OBC Students
fullText:

SHREYAS Strengthens Higher Education Opportunities for SC and OBC Students

Scheme Supports Free Coaching, Education in Premier Institutions, Overseas Studies and Research Fellowships

Rs. 3,509.39 Crore Expenditure Recorded Under Four Components from 2014-15 to 2025-26, benefitting over 1.18 Lakh SC, OBC Students: Dr Virendra Kumar

15 SEP 2026 4:44PM by PIB Delhi

The Central Government is advancing the educational empowerment of students belonging to Scheduled Castes (SCs) and Other Backward Classes (OBCs) through the Scholarships for Higher Education for Young Achievers Scheme (SHREYAS).

Union Minister of Social Justice And Empowerment, Dr Virendra Kumar said that from 2014-15 to 2025-26, a cumulative expenditure of approximately Rs. 3,509.39 crore has been recorded under the four major components of SHREYAS adding that during this period, the cumulative beneficiary count reported under these components was 1,18,248.

The Minister said the Scheme brings together targeted interventions aimed at reducing financial barriers and improving access to academic and professional opportunities. Its major components provide free coaching for competitive examinations, financial assistance for studying in premier institutions, support for higher education abroad and fellowships for advanced research, he added.

Stating that the Free Coaching component provides financial assistance for quality coaching to economically disadvantaged SC and OBC students appearing for competitive and professional examinations, Dr Kumar said the initiative seeks to enable eligible students to compete for admission to reputed educational institutions and secure opportunities in public and private employment.

Dr Kumar informed that between 2014-15 and 2025-26, expenditure of approximately Rs. 145.10 crore was reported under this component, with a cumulative beneficiary count of 23,208. He added that in 2024-25, the expenditure stood at Rs. 17.68 crore, benefiting 2,136 students. During 2025-26, an expenditure of Rs. 9.87 crore was reported, covering 854 beneficiaries, Dr Kumar added..

The Union Minister said the Ministry’s Top Class Education component supports meritorious Scheduled Caste students pursuing studies in premier educational institutions across the country. He said the financial assistance helps eligible students meet the costs associated with quality higher education and pursue professional and academic programmes without being constrained by their economic circumstances.

Dr Kumar further informed that from 2014-15 to 2025-26, approximately Rs. 703.44 crore was spent under this component, with a cumulative beneficiary count of 35,237. He said the annual expenditure increased from Rs. 19.37 crore for 1,568 beneficiaries in 2014-15 to Rs. 117.19 crore for 4,742 beneficiaries in 2025-26 adding that the expenditure recorded during 2025-26 was the highest reported during the period covered.

Describing National Overseas Scholarship Scheme (NOS) as a game changer enabling eligible Scheduled Caste students to pursue higher studies at reputed institutions abroad, Dr Kumar said this Scheme expands access to international academic exposure and advanced educational opportunities for students from socially disadvantaged backgrounds.

The Minister informed that between the selection years 2014-15 and 2025-26, the expenditure of approximately Rs. 461.57 crore was reported under the scheme. He added that during this period, 764 beneficiaries went abroad for higher studies with the number increased from 20 in 2014-15 to a high of 114 in 2023-24. Subsequently, 80 beneficiaries went abroad in 2024-25, while 67 beneficiaries were reported in 2025-26. Expenditure under the component stood at Rs. 54.89 crore in 2025-26, the Minister further said.

The Union Minister said the National Fellowship for SC Students (NFSC) provides financial assistance to Scheduled Caste scholars pursuing higher education and research programmes. He said the fellowship promotes participation in advanced academic research and supports scholars in building careers in teaching, research and other knowledge-based fields.

The Minister stated that from 2014-15 to 2025-26, an expenditure of approximately Rs. 2,199.28 crore was reported under NFSC, with a cumulative beneficiary count of 59,039. He further stated that during 2025-26, the expenditure reached Rs. 213.45 crore, benefiting 4,218 scholars. This represented an increase over 2024-25, when expenditure of Rs. 209.50 crore was reported for 4,143 beneficiaries, he added.

Pertinently, through its four major components, SHREYAS provides a continuum of educational support - from preparation for competitive examinations and access to premier institutions to overseas education and advanced research. The scheme reflects the Government's commitment to promoting equitable access to quality education and enabling young achievers from socially disadvantaged communities to realise their academic and professional aspirations.

headline: Union Minister Dr Jitendra Singh Inaugurates Indigenous SPROUT Facility at BRIC-NIPGR to Accelerate Development of Climate-Resilient Crops
fullText:
Ministry of Science & Technology

Union Minister Dr Jitendra Singh Inaugurates Indigenous SPROUT Facility at BRIC-NIPGR to Accelerate Development of Climate-Resilient Crops

SPROUT will enable crop research under different environmental conditions, helping connect genomics and gene technologies with faster trait evaluation and crop improvement says Dr Jitendra Singh

India witnessing simultaneous advances in plant and human biotechnology as part of BioE3 policy and the biotechnology push of Modi Government: Dr Jitendra Singh

SpeedSeed technology can reduce chickpea generation cycle to around 40 days, considerably shortening breeding timelines: Dr. Jitendra Singh

15 SEP 2026 4:31PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science & Technology and Earth Sciences and MoS PMO, Dr. Jitendra Singh today inaugurated the "SpeedSeed Phenotyping and Resource Optimization for Unified Trait Analysis" (SPROUT) facility at BRIC-National Institute of Plant Genome Research (BRIC-NIPGR), New Delhi, describing it as an important indigenous capability for developing climate-resilient crops suited to different weather conditions.

The Minister said that in a country as geographically and agro-climatically diverse as India, the ability to study and evaluate crops under different environmental conditions is critical for strengthening agricultural resilience. The Minister said the initiative is part of the wider BioE3 policy and the biotechnology push of the Modi Government, under which simultaneous breakthroughs are taking place in plant biotechnology as well as human biotechnology. The BioE3 policy itself includes climate-resilient agriculture among its strategic thematic sectors.

The event was attended by Prof. Manoj Prasad, Director, BRIC-NIPGR; Dr. Senthil K. Muthappa, BRIC-NIPGR; and Dr. Nitin Jain, Scientist-H, Department of Biotechnology (DBT). During the programme, Dr. Jitendra Singh inaugurated the SPROUT facility and planted a sapling under the “Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam” campaign. He also interacted with scientists and officials of BRIC-NIPGR.

SPROUT is a season-independent, controlled-environment facility designed for high-throughput phenotyping, precision stress screening and evaluation of germplasm, breeding populations, mutants, transgenic and genome-edited lines. With a major focus on chickpea, the facility will help connect advances in genomics and genome editing with precise trait evaluation and breeding. This will strengthen the ability to move more efficiently from gene discovery to trait validation and ultimately to crop improvement.

The facility comes at a time when climate change and changing weather patterns are creating an urgent need for faster agricultural solutions. Research supported in agriculture biotechnology has resulted in improved plant varieties and genotypes across economically important crops including rice, wheat, oilseeds, pulses, millets, fruits and vegetables, while work on plant microbiome interactions is opening possibilities for beneficial microorganisms to support sustainable crop productivity, soil health and nutrient availability.

Dr. Jitendra Singh said that modern biotechnology must increasingly be translated into technologies that can respond to real agricultural challenges and provide tangible benefits to farmers. He said that the scientific advances being made today, particularly in genomics, gene technologies, precision phenotyping and accelerated breeding, will become increasingly relevant in the years ahead.

NIPGR has also developed SpeedSeed, a separate technology for accelerated generation advancement. In chickpea, optimised protocols can reduce the generation cycle to approximately 40 days, considerably shortening conventional breeding and research timelines. The technology can be used within SPROUT or adapted to other suitable controlled-environment facilities. Together, SPROUT and SpeedSeed can accelerate the evaluation and advancement of promising crop traits and shorten the path from research to improved varieties.

Over the last twelve years, the Department of Biotechnology has played a transformative role in strengthening India’s agriculture biotechnology ecosystem, supporting innovation from laboratory research to farmers’ fields. Between 2014 and 2026, more than 300 projects were supported in agriculture biotechnology and allied areas. More than 50 improved varieties across rice, wheat, chickpea, mustard, vegetables and forestry species have been developed with enhanced tolerance to drought, floods, salinity, pests and diseases.

A major achievement has been the development of 17 climate-resilient rice varieties under a flagship genomics-assisted breeding programme. These varieties are now cultivated across nearly 15 lakh hectares, demonstrating the potential of advanced genomics and molecular breeding to translate scientific research into solutions with direct relevance to farmers and food security.

The Minister said that the biotechnology ecosystem is expanding beyond individual technologies and laboratories, with advances in plant biotechnology, human biotechnology, genomics and other emerging areas taking place simultaneously. He said that the country’s biotechnology journey is increasingly being driven by the convergence of advanced science, technology and applications that can address challenges relating to agriculture, health, sustainability and national development.

He also referred to the wider role of biotechnology in areas such as genetic technologies and recycling/circular approaches, stressing the need to align institutional capabilities and human-resource systems with the rapidly changing scientific landscape. The BioE3 framework similarly seeks to promote a sustainable and circular bioeconomy through convergence between biotechnology, engineering and digitalisation.

Dr. Jitendra Singh said that scientific achievements should not remain confined to laboratories or scientific institutions and called for a stronger culture of science communication and public outreach. He said that official visits to scientific institutions should not be limited to formal engagement or publicity, but should help those for whom the technologies are being developed understand what is being done and how it benefits them.

He suggested greater use of short films, workshops and professionally produced visual content to explain scientific technologies in an accessible manner. Such communication, he said, could show the challenges that existed before a technology was developed, explain how the scientific intervention addressed those challenges and demonstrate the relief or benefit that the technology has brought to farmers, industry and other users. Technical experts and professional communicators could work together to present these stories in a manner that has greater public and media impact.

The Minister also called for stronger interaction between scientific institutions and industry partners, farmers and other stakeholders. He said that regular institutional meetings and presentations should provide opportunities for people from outside the immediate scientific ecosystem to participate, so that scientists and stakeholders can understand each other’s work and identify opportunities for collaboration.

Referring to the experience of CSIR institutions, Dr. Jitendra Singh said that regular meetings can be used as platforms for scientific presentations and for bringing external stakeholders into discussions. He encouraged BRIC-NIPGR and other institutions to adopt similar practices and involve industry partners and other relevant stakeholders in institutional interactions so that the benefits of scientific research can reach beyond the scientific community.

He also stressed the importance of taking farmers into scientific institutions and allowing them to see the work being carried out there. Recalling his experience with CSIR institutions, the Minister said that farmers who had never previously visited such research establishments could develop misconceptions about the nature of the work being undertaken. Direct interaction and exposure, he said, can remove such apprehensions and help farmers understand how modern science and biotechnology are being developed for their benefit.

Dr. Jitendra Singh also referred to ongoing biotechnology initiatives involving experimental kits and scientific work in this emerging space, including the use of kits from a biotechnology laboratory in Delhi for experiments, and said that such developments should also find appropriate space in the wider communication of India’s biotechnology progress.

He said that institutions must continuously adapt their communication and human-resource practices to current scientific and technological trends, rather than relying only on conventional approaches. Scientific organisations, he added, need to become more vocal and visible in communicating their achievements so that society, industry and potential beneficiaries are aware of the work being undertaken.

The Minister said that the technologies being developed in biotechnology today are futuristic in nature and will become increasingly relevant in the years to come. He called for sustained efforts to communicate these advances in a manner that demonstrates what Indian science is doing for farmers, industry and society.

Facilities such as SPROUT, he said, demonstrate how modern biotechnology can contribute to the development of climate-resilient and productive crops, strengthen India’s agricultural capabilities and support the goal of a more self-reliant agriculture sector. He congratulated the scientists and technical teams of BRIC-NIPGR for developing the facility and said that such capabilities will contribute to India’s journey towards Viksit Bharat 2047.

headline: From Waste Picker to Swachhta Udyami: Balamala Malli's Journey Towards Dignity and Self-Reliance
fullText:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment

From Waste Picker to Swachhta Udyami: Balamala Malli's Journey Towards Dignity and Self-Reliance

15 SEP 2026 4:20PM by PIB Delhi

The limited income, social exclusion and lack of educational opportunities can restrict the possibility of building a secure future for sanitation workers from economically disadvantaged communities. Timely financial assistance and access to mechanised sanitation equipment can help transform such vulnerable livelihoods into safer and more sustainable sources of income.

Demonstrating the impact of support under the Swachhta Udyami Yojana (SUY) component of the NAMASTE Scheme, Shri Balamala Malli, a 30-year-old member of the Scheduled Tribe community, has moved towards greater economic stability and dignity. As part of a five-member group project, he received assistance to procure a 3-in-1 Jetting, Grabbing and Rodding Machine, which created an additional livelihood opportunity for him and the other group members.

Shri Malli has worked as a waste picker with the Guntur Municipal Corporation in Andhra Pradesh, for the past ten years. He worked six days a week and earned approximately Rs. 150 to Rs. 200 per day.

Poverty had prevented Mr. Malli from attending school. His parents were extremely poor, and he began accompanying them in waste-picking activities at a young age instead of receiving a formal education. As an illiterate member of the Scheduled Tribe community living in an urban slum, he also faced social discrimination, exclusion and limited access to essential amenities and services.

His wife is a homemaker, and the couple have three children studying in elementary school. Despite the family's difficult socioeconomic circumstances, Mr. Malli aspired to become economically self-sufficient and provide his children with quality education and a better future.

On 19 June 2023, financial assistance was provided by the National Safai Karamcharis Finance and Development Corporation (NSKFDC) under SUY for a group project comprising Shri Malli and four other members. The support enabled the group to procure a 3-in-1 Jetting, Grabbing and Rodding Machine for mechanised sanitation work.

The project had a total cost of Rs. 49,40,710. It was supported through a loan amount of Rs. 30,80,530 and an upfront capital subsidy of Rs. 18,60,180. Access to the machine enhanced the group's livelihood opportunities and enabled its members to undertake sanitation operations through safer and more efficient mechanical methods.

Before receiving assistance, Shri Malli earned approximately Rs. 8,000 per month through waste-picking activities. Following the procurement of the 3-in-1 machine, he began earning an additional Rs. 10,000 per month, increasing his total monthly income to approximately Rs. 18,000.

The increase in income has enabled Shri Malli to meet household expenses more comfortably, support his children's education and address several of the economic challenges that previously affected his family. The intervention has strengthened his livelihood and helped him lead a more stable and dignified life.

Shri Malli's journey shows how financial assistance, collective enterprise and mechanised sanitation equipment can improve livelihood security for sanitation workers. From relying on low-paid waste-picking work, he has become part of a group enterprise with improved earning opportunities and greater confidence about his family's future.

Talking about the support, Shri Malli said, “The support helped me increase my income and provide better education and a more secure future for my children. I now feel more confident about supporting my family and living with dignity.”

Today, he is working towards economic self-reliance and ensuring that his children receive the education and opportunities that poverty denied him. His progress reflects the role of the SUY component of the NAMASTE Scheme in advancing safety, dignity and sustainable livelihoods among sanitation workers.

headline: Press Note on Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) Monthly Bulletin August 2026
fullText:
Ministry of Statistics & Programme Implementation

Press Note on Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) Monthly Bulletin August 2026

Overall LFPR increased further

WPR strengthened in rural areas and stable in urban areas

Rural UR recorded decline

15 SEP 2026 4:00PM by PIB Delhi

Snapshot: The overall LFPR (15+ years) increased to 55.6% in August, 2026, up from 55.4% in July, 2026. LFPR (15+ years and above) in rural areas stood at 58.2% in August, 2026, registering an increase of 1.2 percentage points over August 2025. Overall female LFPR (15+ years and above) recorded at 34.8% in August, 2026, 1.1 percentage points higher than the level recorded in August, 2025. Overall WPR (15+ years and above) increased to 52.8% in August 2026,the highest level recorded since March, 2026. Rural WPR (15+ years and above) increased by 1.3 percentage points year-on-year to 55.8% in August, 2026. Overall UR (15+ years and above) remained stable at 5.0% in August, 2026. Rural UR declined to 4.1% in August, 2026, the lowest level recorded since January 2026.

The Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) conducted by NSO, MoSPI, is the primary source of data on activity participation and employment and unemployment conditions of the population. The PLFS survey methodology has been modified from January, 2025 to provide monthly and quarterly estimates of labour force indicators for the country.

Monthly results of PLFS are released in the form of Monthly Bulletins. It presents estimates of key labour market indicators viz. Labour Force Participation Rate (LFPR), Worker Population Ratio (WPR) and Unemployment Rate (UR) at the all-India level following the Current Weekly Status[1] (CWS) approach.

The Monthly Bulletins for April, 2025 to July, 2026 have already been released. The present Monthly Bulletin for August, 2026 is the seventeenth in the series.

Key findings for persons of age 15 years and above following CWS:

Labour Force Participation Rate (LFPR) strengthened:

The overall Labour Force Participation Rate (LFPR) for persons aged 15 years and above increased to 55.6% in August, 2026, from 55.4% in July, 2026. A similar trend has also been observed in rural areas, where the LFPR for persons aged 15 years and above increased to 58.2% in August, 2026, from 58.0% in July, 2026. In urban areas, LFPR remained constant at 50.4% in August, 2026 as compared to the previous month.

Compared to the corresponding month of the previous year, the overall LFPR increased by 0.6 percentage point, from 55.0% in August, 2025 to 55.6% in August, 2026. During the same period, rural LFPR also increased by 1.2 percentage points, from 57.0% to 58.2%, while urban LFPR experienced a marginal decline of 0.5 percentage point, from 50.9% to 50.4%.

Rural LFPR registered an increase of 1.2 percentage points over the corresponding month of the previous year, reaching 58.2% in August, 2026

Female Labour Force Participation exhibits upward momentum:

The overall female LFPR experienced a moderate increase from 34.4% in July, 2026 to 34.8% in August, 2026 mainly contributed by rural female LFPR which increased to 39.4% during the current month from 38.8% recorded in the previous month. During the same period, female LFPR in urban areas was broadly stable at 25.4% compared to 25.3% observed in July, 2026.

Over the year, the overall female LFPR increased by 1.1 percentage points, from 33.7% in August, 2025 to 34.8% in August, 2026. During the same period, female LFPR in rural areas increased by 2.0 percentage points, from 37.4% to 39.4%, while urban female LFPR declined by 0.7 percentage point, from 26.1% to 25.4%.

Overall female LFPR increased for the second consecutive month, reaching 34.8% in August 2026

Rise in rural workforce participation across genders:

The overall WPR increased from 52.5% in July, 2026 to 52.8% in August, 2026 driven by increased workforce participation in rural areas. WPR in rural areas recorded an increase to 55.8% in August, 2026 from 55.4% in the previous month while urban WPR maintained the same level of 47.0% in August, 2026 as observed in July, 2026.

The overall WPR showing an increase of 0.6 percentage point over the corresponding month of the previous year from 52.2% in August, 2025 to 52.8% in August, 2026. During the same period, rural WPR increased by 1.3 percentage points from 54.5% to 55.8%, whereas the urban WPR stood at 47.0% in August, 2026 from 47.5% in August, 2025, experienced a decline of 0.5 percentage point.

Year-on-year comparison indicates an increase in the overall female WPR, rising to 33.0% in August, 2026 from 32.0% recorded in August, 2025.

Rural Unemployment Rate (UR) declined:

Overall UR among persons of age 15 years and above declined marginally from 5.1% in July, 2026 to 5.0% in August, 2026. During the same period, rural UR decreased from 4.5% to 4.1%, while urban UR remained almost stable at 6.8% in August, 2026 compared to 6.7% in July, 2026.

Compared with August, 2025, the overall UR and urban UR remained broadly stable in August, 2026, whereas the rural UR declined by 0.2 percentage point from 4.3% in August, 2025 to 4.1% in August, 2026.

Since January, 2026, rural UR recorded its lowest level of 4.1% in August, 2026

Rural UR decreased across gender:

The overall UR among male aged 15 years and above declined for the three consecutive months, reaching 4.9% in August, 2026 from 5.4% in May, 2026. The rural male UR declined from 4.6% in July, 2026 to 4.3% in August, 2026, while urban male UR marginally up from 5.9% to 6.1% during the same period. Among female of age 15 years and above, overall UR declined in two consecutive months to 5.1% in August, 2026 from 5.9% in June, 2026. Rural female UR decreased from 4.3% in July, 2026 to 3.9% in August, 2026 while urban female UR remained broadly stable compared to previous month.

A year-on-year comparison indicates that the overall UR for both male and female remained broadly unchanged in August, 2026.

The overall male and female UR declined in August, 2026 compared to July, 2026

At the all-India level, the monthly estimates are based on information collected from a total number of 3,70,160 persons surveyed.

headline: From Financial Barriers to Doctoral Achievement: Shewani Kumari's Journey towards Academic Excellence
fullText:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment

From Financial Barriers to Doctoral Achievement: Shewani Kumari's Journey towards Academic Excellence

15 SEP 2026 3:41PM by PIB Delhi

Financial help and support can make higher education and advanced research feasible and possible for students from socially and economically disadvantaged backgrounds. Fellowship assistance can provide the stability required to meet academic expenses, continue research and work towards long-term professional goals.

Shewani Kumari, a 29-year-old scholar from the Scheduled Caste community, overcame financial, social and educational barriers to complete her Ph.D. in Sociology. She is presently working as a lecturer and aspires to become an Assistant Professor.

Coming from a family with limited income, Shewani faced considerable difficulty in meeting the costs of higher education and research. Expenses related to tuition, books, research materials, travel and other academic activities placed a significant burden on the family and created uncertainty about the continuation of her studies.

Limited access to academic resources, professional guidance and quality educational opportunities added to these challenges. Social and geographical limitations also restricted her exposure to advanced academic and career opportunities.

Despite these barriers, Shewani remained committed to her education. She viewed academic achievement as a means of building a better future for her family and improving its socio-economic condition through professional success.

Financial assistance through the NFSDC Fellowship for Higher Education and Research became an important source of support in her academic journey. She received Rs. 31,000 per month as a Junior Research Fellow and Rs. 35,000 per month as a Senior Research Fellow.

The fellowship helped her meet essential educational and research expenses and enabled her to continue her work with greater financial stability. It also provided encouragement and strengthened her confidence to pursue her academic goals.

With the support of the fellowship and her sustained determination, Shewani successfully completed her Ph.D. in Sociology and gained teaching experience. These achievements have strengthened her academic and professional position.

At present, Shewani is working as a lecturer and progressing towards her aspiration of becoming an Assistant Professor. Her journey demonstrates how timely financial assistance can enable scholars from disadvantaged communities to overcome structural barriers and pursue advanced education.

Expressing her wish to move ahead for next level in professional career, Shewani Kumari said, “The fellowship gave me the financial support and confidence to continue my research and complete my Ph.D. Today, as a lecturer, I am closer to fulfilling my dream of becoming an Assistant Professor and creating a better future through education."

Shewani's success reflects the transformative role of fellowship support in expanding access to research and professional opportunities. Her achievement is an example of perseverance strengthened by institutional assistance and educational opportunity.

headline: From Addiction and Distress to Recovery and Stability: Dev M's Journey through Counselling and Rehabilitation
fullText:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment

From Addiction and Distress to Recovery and Stability: Dev M's Journey through Counselling and Rehabilitation

15 SEP 2026 2:58PM by PIB Delhi

Addiction can affect not only an individual's health but also family relationships, livelihood, emotional well-being and social standing. Timely counselling, medical treatment and sustained follow-up can help a person understand addiction-related triggers, develop healthier coping mechanisms and move steadily towards recovery and rehabilitation.

Demonstrating the value of coordinated rehabilitation support, Dev M (name changed), a 29-year-old self-employed man from the OBC community in Akola district, Maharashtra, received counselling and medical treatment through the Purogami Bhaiyyuprasad Samaj Kalyan Vikas Vyayam Prasark Sanstha, an Integrated Rehabilitation Centre for Addicts (IRCA). The intervention helped strengthen his recovery process and contributed positively to his overall well-being.

Before receiving support, Dev was facing multiple family, financial and social challenges that had significantly affected his personal and professional life. Addiction contributed to financial difficulties, and its adverse impact was also reflected in the performance of his business and his overall economic stability.

Frequent family conflicts and strained relationships created an emotionally stressful environment for Dev and those around him. At the same time, social stigma and disrespectful treatment affected his mental well-being and weakened his confidence. These combined pressures made it more difficult for him to regain stability in his personal life and livelihood.

Despite these challenges, Dev aspired to overcome addiction completely, improve his family relationships and lead a peaceful and stable life. He also wanted to develop better emotional control and seek support from trusted individuals whenever he faced stress or difficulties.

On 5 October 2025, Dev received support through the IRCA in Akola. As part of the rehabilitation process, he was provided free medical treatment, psychological therapy, family counselling, addiction-related medicines, free food during treatment and regular follow-up services.

Through individual, group and family counselling sessions, Dev received guidance to address his personal challenges and recognise the triggers associated with addiction. The sessions also helped him understand how stress, strained relationships and emotional difficulties could influence his behaviour and recovery.

Dev was introduced to practical stress-management techniques, including deep-breathing exercises, maintaining a daily activity diary and engaging in regular physical exercise. He was also encouraged to discuss his concerns with trusted individuals instead of facing difficult situations alone. These measures supported the development of healthier responses to stress and addiction-related triggers.

Counselling and medical treatment provided the structured support required to facilitate his recovery and rehabilitation. Family counselling helped address strained relationships, while regular follow-up reinforced the guidance received during treatment and strengthened his commitment to the recovery process.

The intervention has contributed positively to Dev's overall well-being and helped him move towards better emotional control, improved family relations and a more stable life. Continued counselling, medical care and follow-up support have remained important components of his rehabilitation journey.

Talking about the facilitation, Dev M expressed his views, “Counselling and medical care helped me gain better emotional control, improve my family relationships and move towards a more stable life.”

Dev's experience highlights how accessible treatment, psychological support, family participation and regular follow-up can help individuals facing addiction work towards recovery with dignity. His journey reflects the importance of timely institutional support in enabling beneficiaries to rebuild confidence, restore relationships and move towards a peaceful and productive future.

headline: Astronomy enthusiasts from across India participate in the fourth HDSR Star Party
fullText:
Ministry of Science & Technology

Astronomy enthusiasts from across India participate in the fourth HDSR Star Party

15 SEP 2026 2:56PM by PIB Delhi

Expert astrophotographers and amateur astronomers from across the country participated in the fourth edition of the Hanle Dark Sky Reserve Star Party from 7 – 12 September, 2026 at the Indian Astronomical Observatory in Hanle, Ladakh.

“The enthusiasm with which amateur astronomers as well as astrophotographers from across the country participated, highlighted the event’s role in underlining the importance of preserving its pristine dark skies, both for scientific research and for the public, said Prof. Annapurni Subramaniam, Director of IIA.

Around 40 amateur astronomers from Chandigarh, Goa, Gujarat, Haryana, Himachal Pradesh, Karnataka, Maharashtra, New Delhi, Madhya Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Rajasthan, and Uttar Pradesh. These selected participants travelled to Leh with their advanced equipment, to fully utilise the four nights under the dark skies of Hanle at the event organised jointly by the Indian Institute of Astrophysics (IIA), Department of Wildlife Protection of UT Ladakh, Bhabha Atomic Research Centre (BARC), and the Tata Institute of Fundamental Research (TIFR).

The Open Night for the local communities and the nearby tourists on 10th September saw footfalls of more than 1200 people.

The Star Party participants, along with the HDSR Astronomy Ambassadors and the Observatory staff showed the visitors through specially designated amateur telescopes and answered their myriad questions throughout the evening. Senior officials from various organisations in the area were also invited to look through telescopes and were briefed on the importance of curtailing light pollution in the region.

Special training sessions were organised every evening for the HDSR Astronomy Ambassadors, the 25 local villagers who have been trained to conduct astronomy tours for tourists for the past three years, and who have been supplied with telescopes by the government of Ladakh. The expert participants also acted as mentors and helped in teaching many practical aspects of night sky watching and astrophotography to the Ambassadors.

The Hanle Dark Sky Reserve (HDSR) in Ladakh is renowned for its exceptionally dark night sky, making it a highly attractive location for astrophotographers and amateur astronomers. Notified as a dark sky reserve by the Government of Ladakh in December 2022, HDSR represents a novel astronomy based socio-economic development initiative. It is built on two key concepts: reducing light pollution for the benefit of continued research at the Observatory, and promoting astro-tourism that creates benefits for local communities.

The success of HDSR is enabled by the strong commitment of various stakeholders, including the UT Ladakh administration. HDSR is anchored by the Indian Astronomical Observatory at Hanle. The Observatory is operated by the IIA, an autonomous institution under the Department of Science and Technology (DST).

The annual HDSR Star Party underscores the importance of preserving the dark skies of Hanle for the future, and the diverse set of stakeholders for whom the Hanle skies are a vital and rare resource. “With the 3.7-m upgraded Himalayan Chandra Telescope and the 13.7-m National Large Optical-infrared Telescope that are proposed to come up in Hanle, it is imperative that we come together to safeguard its dark skies”, said Prof DK Sahu of IIA, Scientist in charge of the Observatory.

headline: ‘VIMARSH’ DRDO-Industry Synergy Meet: Raksha Mantri unveils key policy initiatives to empower MSMEs & start-ups and launches framework to share software source codes with licensee industries
fullText:
Ministry of Defence

‘VIMARSH’ DRDO-Industry Synergy Meet: Raksha Mantri unveils key policy initiatives to empower MSMEs & start-ups and launches framework to share software source codes with licensee industries

Nine Licensing Agreements for Transfer of Technology handed over to 13 manufacturing partners; MoUs exchanged to expand industry outreach

Need to expand DRDO-Industry collaboration, integrate MSMEs & start-ups as integral parts into defence supply chain to transform India into a global production hub: Shri Rajnath Singh

“Viksit Bharat goal is to build an economically strong, technologically self-reliant, socially inclusive, environmentally sustainable & strategically secure nation”

15 SEP 2026 1:45PM by PIB Delhi

Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh unveiled key policy initiatives during ‘VIMARSH’, a DRDO-Industry Synergy Meet, in New Delhi on September 15, 2026. The initiatives include a comprehensive framework to lower technical and financial entry barriers for MSMEs & deep-tech start-ups, offering direct funding, incubation support and dedicated access to DRDO testing facilities. A standardised, secure framework for sharing DRDO-developed software source codes with licensee industries was also launched to accelerate software-defined defence capabilities and obsolescence management.

Nine (09) Licensing Agreements for Transfer of Technology (LAToTS) were handed over to 13 manufacturing partners in the presence of Raksha Mantri to enable commercial production of state-of-the-art systems.

List of LAToTs handed over to Industry

Strategic MoUs were also formally exchanged with the Society of Indian Defence Manufacturers (SIDM) and Laghu Udyog Bharati (LUB) to expand industry outreach and foster grass-roots participation. DRDO also signed a contract with Quality Council of India for System for Advance Manufacturing Assessment and Rating (SAMAR) version 2.0 to benchmark the manufacturing maturity of domestic defence enterprises.

In his address, Raksha Mantri asserted that the DRDO-Industry collaboration should no longer be limited to production alone, but expanded across the entire value chain encompassing research, design, testing, certification, and manufacturing to transform India into a global hub for defence manufacturing. “DRDO possesses knowledge and technology, the industry has scale and manufacturing capability, start-ups bring innovation and agility, and the youth hold the dream of a New India. When these four forces converge and move forward together, no goal is impossible,” he said.

Shri Rajnath Singh underlined that the goal of Viksit Bharat is not merely to build an economically strong nation, but to also make it technologically self-reliant, socially inclusive, environmentally sustainable, and strategically secure. “By 2047, we must achieve Aatmanirbharta in critical technologies, a significant increase in indigenous content, multi-fold growth in defence exports, and a robust presence for India in global supply chains,” he said.

Raksha Mantri enumerated the unprecedented reforms brought about in the defence sector over the past few years under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, including the notification of Positive Indigenisation Lists, ‘Make in India’ initiative, iDEX, ADITI, and the decision to allocate 25% of the defence R&D budget to the private sector to reduce import dependence and move towards self-reliance. He added that grants are being provided to start-ups through the Technology Development Fund, and numerous technologies have already reached the production stage. He highlighted that iDEX has also created a new ecosystem for defence innovation, where start-ups are developing solutions based on actual operational requirements.

Describing start-ups and MSMEs as the new flag-bearers of innovation in India, Shri Rajnath Singh stated that these industries play a pivotal role in achieving the goal of Aatmanirbhar Bharat as they develop components, sub-systems etc. for major defence systems alongside state-of-the-art technologies. He underscored the need to integrate MSMEs and start-ups as integral parts into the defence supply chain alongside large industries, expressing confidence that the new initiatives would create fresh opportunities for industry.

Raksha Mantri highlighted that the new policy initiatives focus on promoting industry-led R&D; providing funding and mentorship to start-ups and MSMEs; fostering academia-industry collaboration; and encouraging investment in futuristic technologies such as AI, quantum computing, hypersonics, and directed energy.

Shri Rajnath Singh stated that as India is rapidly transitioning from a defence importer to an exporter, there are a number of sectors such as drone technology, AI and cyber security where the MSMEs and start-ups can accelerate innovation, and elevate India’s technological and strategic strengths to newer heights. “MSMEs are the backbone of the Indian economy and a critical strength of the defence ecosystem. They need to consistently focus on quality, delivery, innovation, and global standards, while expanding partnerships with large companies,” he said.

Raksha Mantri emphasised that a nation that possesses its own technology holds the power to shape its own future, adding that self-reliance must become an integral part of the country’s character and attitude. “Companies that invest in new and emerging technologies today will become the leaders of tomorrow as in future warfare, the country that leads in technology will secure the strategic advantage,” he added.

Speaking on the occasion, Defence Secretary and Secretary, Department of Defence R&D and Chairman, DRDO Shri Rajesh Kumar Singh said VIMARSH 2026, centered on the theme ‘Varta se Vikas’, has been strategically designed to align cutting-edge commercial innovation with national defence readiness and systematically integrate private sector capabilities into the core of the defence ecosystem. This forum serves as a key vehicle for transforming the national security framework from a mere transactional buyer-seller relationship into a collaborative, co-created technology ecosystem, he said.

Shri Rajesh Kumar Singh also highlighted the transformation witnessed by the defence sector in the recent years due to the Government’s self-reliance efforts. “The expansion of technology transfer has not only facilitated the establishment of parallel production lines to meet the Defence Forces’ requirements, thereby directly benefiting MSMEs, but has also helped alleviate the constraints that previously hindered a limited manufacturing base. Till date, over 2,300 Technology Transfers (ToTs) have been handed over to more than 1,100 industries. Currently, we have made technologies related to approximately 50 missiles, developed by DRDO, available to the industry to foster increased participation,” he added.

A book titled ‘Defence Systems for Resilient Bharat – Advancing Aatmanirbharta in Defence’, a special compilation documenting significant defence systems developed by DRDO’s technology clusters between 2014 to 2026 was also released during the event, along with the guidelines for Human Resource Outsourcing Service Contracts in DRDO. The guidelines provide a comprehensive framework for formulation of service specifications for the procurement, selection of suitable service providers, contract administration, performance monitoring and compliance with contractual as well as statutory obligations for Human Resource Outsourcing across DRDO labs.

Secretary (Defence Production) Shri Sanjeev Kumar, Secretary (Defence Finance) Shri Vishvajit Sahay and Distinguished Scientist & Director General (Production Coordination & Services Interaction), DRDO Dr (Smt) Chandrika Kaushik were present on the occasion.

During the Technical Sessions, Directors General of DRDO Technological Clusters outlined technical roadmaps across Aeronautical Systems, Missiles, Armaments, Microelectronics, and Naval Systems. DRDO HQ introduced initiatives aimed at simplifying procedural compliance, fast-tracking facility access, and compressing licensing timelines.

In the High-Level Panel Discussion, senior representatives from DRDO, Department of Defence Production (DDP), and the Defence Forces deliberated on mechanisms for accelerating technology absorption, optimising Development-cum-Production Partner models, and ensuring rapid induction of indigenous technologies into active service.

The flagship event was attended by over 250 defence industry leaders, industry chamber representatives, senior civil and military officials and senior DRDO scientists. Secretary, DPIIT also participated in the meet. Designed to strengthen the national defence-industrial framework, VIMARSH 2026 provided a structured platform to align DRDO’s technological research and emerging deep-tech startups with the established manufacturing ecosystem, creating an agile, transparent, and collaborative environment for private sector participation.

headline: Union Minister Dr. Jitendra Singh to launch dedicated web-portal for Special Campaign 6 on 16th September, 2026
fullText:
